_meta.title: Harborlight parent digest
_meta.source: Harborlight Montessori school emails (Notes from Marcy and Dorah, school-wide announcements, classroom notes), summarized
_meta.notes: Summaries transcribed from school emails. Children are referred to by first name only. No class rosters, home addresses, phone numbers, or billing details. Items are newest first. 'partial' confidence means the source page could not be fully verified.

items.title: Whalemobile visit and back-to-school logistics
items.summary: A 43-foot inflatable Whalemobile visits Monday so each class can step inside and learn whale anatomy, closing out the summer Ocean Unit with crafts and temporary tattoos. Marcy lays out the end-of-summer and back-to-school schedule. The September 2 Class Visit and Popsicle Party welcomes the new year, with new and transitioning families arriving at 10:00 a.m. and returning families between 10:30 a.m. and noon.

keyDates.label: Whalemobile visits each class (Monday)
Last day of Summer Program (Infant/Toddler and Children's House)
Teacher Prep Week begins, school closed through Aug 28
Classroom Visit Day and Popsicle Party, 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.
First day of school
Labor Day, school closed

actionItems: Bring extra clothing, nap items, and indoor shoes for the first day, and label all items
New and transitioning families arrive at 10:00 a.m. on September 2; returning families arrive between 10:30 a.m. and noon

items.title: Summer vacation show-and-tell and garden donations
items.summary: Marcy invites children to bring one photo or small keepsake from a summer outing for a vacation show-and-tell, noting the no-toy policy, to build public speaking and listening skills. She asks families to donate used coffee grounds in sealed containers and washed, dried eggshells for the garden program. She also describes the snack preparation program that lets children wash, slice, and serve simple snacks.

keyDates.label: Last day of Infant/Toddler and Children's House Summer Program
Teacher Prep Week begins, school closed through Aug 28
First day of school for all students
Labor Day, school closed

actionItems: Send one photo or small keepsake from a summer vacation for show-and-tell (no toys)
Donate used coffee grounds in sealed containers
Donate washed and dried eggshells with the inner membrane removed

items.title: Halfway through summer and back-to-school dates
items.summary: With summer past its midpoint, Marcy shares the back-to-school calendar and asks families to support the garden program. Families can donate used coffee grounds in sealed bags or clean containers and washed, dried eggshells, which students grind with mortars and pestles into the garden soil. She notes the school is expanding the Kindergarten Capstone Program, enhancing garden areas, and adding parent volunteer opportunities.

keyDates.label: Last day of Summer Program
Teacher Prep Week begins, school closed through Aug 28
Class Visit and Popsicle Party, 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. (Wednesday)

actionItems: Donate used coffee grounds in sealed bags or clean recyclable containers
Donate washed, dried eggshells rinsed with the inner membrane removed and air-dried overnight

items.title: Summer Session 2 begins and Shark Week
items.summary: Summer Session 2 opens with the Ocean Unit continuing into a Shark Week theme, and Friday brings shark temporary tattoos with the picnic and popsicles (parents may opt out by emailing the teacher). CH3 and CH4 are no longer merged, so CH4 returns to its own classroom. Marcy reminds families about snack sign-ups, Friday cold-lunch picnics with no-microwave finger foods, and water play day gear.

items.title: 26th Annual Beverly MomBall Tournament
items.summary: The 26th Annual Beverly MomBall Tournament runs September 18 to 20, 2026, and Harborlight's team, the Honey Badgers, invites current and incoming mothers to play in this community fundraiser for Beverly Public Schools and Beverly Bootstraps. No softball experience is needed. Practices are at Herlihy Park, 10 Livingstone Ave. in Beverly, on Thursdays at 6:00 p.m. and Saturdays at 9:30 a.m., with at least one practice a week. Assistant coaching, team sponsorships, and cheer squad spots are also available.

keyDates.label: Deadline to commit to play (sets roster size)

MomBall championship games

actionItems: Players commit by August 15 so organizers can set roster size
Attend at least one practice a week (Thursdays 6:00 p.m., Saturdays 9:30 a.m. at Herlihy Park)
Optional: volunteer as assistant coach, sponsor a team, or join the cheer squad

Marcy asks parents to sign up on the Summer Session 2 snack calendars for CH1 through CH7 and notes that CH3 and CH4 are no longer merged, so CH4 returns to its own classroom. items.title: Children kept indoors for air quality alert
items.summary: Due to an air quality alert, all children stayed indoors for the full day. The school provided indoor activities and said outdoor time would resume once air quality returned to healthy levels. Staff monitored conditions throughout the day.

keyDates.label: Children kept indoors due to air quality alert

items.title: Salem Sound Coastwatch Marvelous Mollusks visit
items.summary: CH5 welcomed Salem Sound Coastwatch for their Marvelous Mollusks program. The children learned about shelled creatures including clams, mussels, oysters, and snails. They did hands-on activities, building mussel structures out of foam, exploring how clams hide from predators, and learning about spiral shell patterns. The teacher shared a Google folder with photos from the day.

keyDates.label: Salem Sound Coastwatch classroom visit

items.title: CH5 weekly recap and reminders
items.summary: CH5 shared highlights from the week: the children made ocean scenery crafts, planted the first seeds in the new class garden, played in the rain when scheduled water play was rained out, and held their first class picnic with lunch outside and popsicles. Photos were attached, along with several supply reminders for families.
actionItems: Send inside shoes for your child
Label all clothing, shoes, water bottles, and belongings
Send a water bottle every day
Keep a complete change of spare clothes at school
On Fridays pack a no-warming lunch for the outdoor picnic
On Tuesdays send a bathing suit, towel, and water shoes for Water Play
Apply sunscreen before school; staff reapply in the afternoon

items.title: Ocean Unit invertebrates and Marvelous Mollusks
items.summary: The weekly Ocean Unit theme is invertebrates, covering octopuses, crabs, sea stars, and squids. Salem Sound Coastwatch runs its Marvelous Mollusks program on Monday July 13 and Tuesday July 14, with staggered 45-minute sessions by classroom. Marcy reminds parents that children need closed-toe, supportive shoes for outdoor play rather than sandals or Crocs, and shares a homemade play dough recipe.

actionItems: Send children in tennis shoes or other closed-toe, supportive shoes for outdoor play, not sandals or Crocs

items.title: Ocean Unit kickoff and first Picnic Friday
items.summary: The summer Ocean Unit begins with a week on fish, using matching cards, nomenclature cards, and counting activities. The first Picnic and Popsicle Day is Friday, so parents should pack a cold, no-microwave finger-food lunch, which continues every Friday through summer. Marcy notes aerosol sunscreen is prohibited by child care regulations and that Salem Sound Coastwatch's Marvelous Mollusks program visits July 13 and 14.

items.title: Welcoming new students and the summer Ocean Unit
items.summary: The week welcomes new and transitioning students to Children's House and launches Kindergarten Skills with a full cohort, opening the summer Ocean Unit with a song about the five oceans. Marcy shares snack sign-up calendars, each class's water play day, and the Friday picnic-and-popsicle routine of no-microwave finger foods. The note lists a full first-day packing checklist and asks for garden plant donations.

items.title: March with Harborlight in the North Shore Pride Parade
items.summary: Harborlight invited families to march in the North Shore Pride Parade on Saturday, June 27 in Salem. The group met at 11:30 a.m. at Shetland Park, 27 Congress Street, Salem, ahead of the noon step-off, and the route ended at Salem Common. Harborlight provided rainbow face paint and swag including necklaces, flags, and pencils. The event ran rain or shine with no rain date.

keyDates.label: Pride Parade at noon; Harborlight group meets 11:30 a.m. in Salem

actionItems: Meet the Harborlight group at 11:30 a.m. at 27 Congress Street, Salem
Wear bright, colorful attire or a Harborlight Pride shirt

items.title: CH6 photos from the year
items.summary: The CH6 teacher shared a Google Drive folder with all the photos taken over the course of the year, since uploading them to the school platform was not working. Families are invited to view the year's activities and to reach out with any trouble accessing the drive.
actionItems: View the CH6 year-in-photos Google Drive folder; contact the teacher if you cannot access it

items.title: End of year, Move Up Ceremony, and summer Ocean Unit preview
items.summary: Marcy closes the school year and invites families to the Move Up Ceremony on Wednesday June 17 at 9:00 a.m., followed by a library reception, on what is also the last day of school. She previews the eight-week summer Ocean Unit that begins June 29, running weekly themes from ocean basics through ocean layers. The school is closed June 18 through June 26 and on July 3.

Each classroom has its own conference day from June 8 to June 12, with sign-up links provided. She welcomes three new team members joining across the classrooms and lists the end-of-year events.
